results.rationale: AI identifies investor concern over Amazon AI capex and free-cash-flow pressure after earnings.
results.ai_headline: Amazon sold off as investors repriced its $200 billion AI capex plan and weaker free-cash-flow outlook.
results.ai_excerpt:
AMZN’s Feb. 3–6 move looks like a coherent AI-capex repricing rather than a random four-day drift: the stock fell each session, from $238.62 on Feb. 3 to $210.32 on Feb. 6, with the largest daily leg on Feb. 6 after earnings and the two internal rolling signals both pointing down (-6.68% for Feb. 3–5 and -9.73% for Feb. 4–6) [1]. The pre-earnings weakness was already visible on Feb. 5, when AMZN closed down 4.42% at $222.69 amid a broader tech/AI selloff and investor focus on AWS growth, AI capex, and guidance ahead of results [2]. The post-close earnings release then supplied the firm-specific catalyst: Amazon reported strong headline growth—Q4 net sales up 14% to $213.4 billion and AWS sales up 24%—but also said free cash flow fell to $11.2 billion from $38.2 billion, mainly due to higher property and equipment spending tied to AI, and guided to about $200 billion of 2026 capex [3].

results.ai_headline: Apple fell as Siri AI delay concerns and an FTC warning hit amid a broader AI-led tech selloff.
results.ai_excerpt:
Apple’s -7.16% rolling move from February 11 to February 13 looks like one coherent selloff rather than a reversal: AAPL was at a $275.50 prior close before a roughly 5% drop on February 12, then continued lower on February 13 from a $261.73 prior close to about $255.78, down another 2.3% [1][2]. The dominant catalyst was firm-specific: after the February 11 close, Bloomberg reported that Apple’s long-planned Siri upgrade had hit internal-testing snags and that features expected for iOS 26.4 could slip into later releases such as iOS 26.5 or iOS 27 [3]. That directly challenged the Apple Intelligence/Siri product-timing narrative; Evercore ISI reportedly expected Apple Intelligence 2.0 to be delayed from March, even while keeping an Outperform rating and $330 target [4].

The main firm-specific catalyst was Airbnb’s February 12 Q4/FY25 report: revenue rose 12% year over year, gross booking value rose 16%—its fastest GBV growth in more than two years—and nights and seats booked rose 10%, while management guided Q1 revenue to $2.59–$2.63 billion and said full-year 2026 revenue growth should accelerate to at least low double digits [2]. results.ai_headline: Tesla rallied on UBS upgrade and AI-chip optimism, amplified by a broad growth-stock relief rally.
results.ai_excerpt:
Tesla’s April 13–16 move looks like a **coherent upside episode concentrated on April 14–15**, not a selloff/reversal: TSLA rose +0.99% to $352.42 on April 13, +3.34% to $364.20 on April 14, then +7.62% to $391.95 on April 15 on 113.8 million shares, before a modest -0.78% pullback to $388.90 on April 16 [1]. That path matches the two positive rolling signals: the strongest move was the April 13–15 +11.22% run, while the April 14–16 +6.78% signal shows the move largely held despite the final-day fade [1].

The firm-specific catalyst mix was strongest. UBS upgraded Tesla on April 14 from Sell to Neutral, saying the post-pullback valuation created a more balanced risk/reward while still flagging weak EV demand, higher investment needs, and slow progress in robotaxi/Optimus [2].
